main_body: A square hay bale drawn as a flat yellow panel with a dark vertical binding strap down the middle and horizontal tie lines, seen face-on. Rows 2-14.
top_band: none: the column runs from the outline (row 2) through light yellow #d4b05c (rows 3-7) to a dark line at row 8, then a mid-tone yellow below. The light region is as tall as the face and is one half of a flat panel, not a separate top surface.
evidence: The bale is a square panel split into an upper light half (rows 3-7) and a lower half (rows 9-14) by a dark horizontal band at row 8, with a vertical strap down the middle. This reads as a front view with straps, not as a top over a front face. The light rows are not set off from the face by a step of 25 L or more, and no front-edge line or eave shadow exists. Both halves are the same straw material and are laid out like two panels. No horizontal surface is visible from above, so it fails the 3/4 contract as a front elevation.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 6 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile, against 17-20 for the references and 38-40 distinct colours. The shading ramp is shallow, with about 3 straw tones (light, mid, dark) plus a dark strap. The outline is a tinted dark brown-olive, which matches the material, and the 0% neutral edge share confirms that. There is some dotted straw texture and no 5x5 flat fills. It is still much thinner and flatter than the references, so it fails.
